page: Microsoft Azure F8-2ams_v7 is a constrained-core virtual machine powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system allocates 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs operating at clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz. Its hardware architecture includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache per core cluster. Advanced instruction extensions are available, including AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16), alongside cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance is paired with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a substantial memory density of 32.0 GB per core. It includes no bundled local storage and contains zero GPUs.

Benchmark results highlight exceptional single-threaded compute efficiency alongside predictable multi-core limitations. The instance achieves top-tier results in stress-ng single-core execution, Geekbench single-core performance (score of 2865.0), single-threaded gzip compression (38.86 GB/sec), and single-threaded bzip3 decompression (17.39 GB/sec). Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth registers at 51.07 GB/sec, while Redis SET performance achieves 6.96 million operations per second. However, total throughput is capped by the two-vCPU ceiling, placing multi-threaded compression, Clang software compilation, and ray tracing in the bottom quartile of evaluated systems.

The F8-2ams_v7 delivers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive environments where commercial database software is licensed on a per-core basis. By bundling 64.0 GB of RAM with only two physical cores, organizations can minimize core license exposure while retaining significant memory headroom. Primary tradeoffs include the complete absence of local ephemeral disks, which requires reliance on network-attached storage volumes, and low parallel processing throughput for compute-bound tasks. Recommended workloads include relational databases, memory caching tiers, ETL parsing, and text-processing services.
